title: WHEN SYNTHETIC USERS FAIL: A CROSS-DOMAIN BENCHMARK OF LLM-SIMULATED HUMAN SURVEY RESPONSES

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the variance in simulated survey responses explained by political views and party identification against real human data from the General Social Survey (GSS) using a stereotyping index (Δη²).
Measuring demographic over-determination based on country of origin using data from the World Values Survey (WVS) by calculating the gap-inflation factor and stereotyping index.
Evaluating demographic over-determination by assessing how much LLMs exaggerate the predictive power of educational attainment (highest degree/education level) on survey responses.
Assessing algorithmic stereotyping by comparing how strongly respondent sex predicts survey answers in LLMs versus real human populations across both GSS and WVS datasets.
Measuring the stereotyping index (Δη²) and Cramér's V to quantify how much LLMs over-associate survey responses with race compared to actual human baselines in the GSS dataset.
Computing the variation in survey answers explained by age group in models versus real humans to identify exaggerated demographic splits.
